summary: Two important findings: (1) GNN encoder produces a single static embedding per article rather than the P time-varying embeddings the paper specifies, losing temporal evolution of neighborhood representations. (2) Student's t NLL loss normalization uses batch-mean df instead of per-element df, producing incorrect gradients for the degrees-of-freedom parameter. Both taxonomy semantic checks pass.

findings.description: The paper produces time-varying GNN embeddings G_i in R^{D x P} by running the GNN encoder at each of the P context timestamps (Section 3.3: 'The embeddings generated by the last GNN layer are denoted as G_i = (g_i^{t-P+1}, ..., g_i^t)'). The implementation runs the GNN once with flattened node features (P demand lags + in-degree as a single vector per node), producing one static embedding per article that is broadcast across all T=P+K time steps. This simplification loses the temporal evolution of neighborhood embeddings — the paper's GNN captures how each article's neighborhood demand dynamics change across timestamps, while the code captures a single snapshot. The acceptable_approximations list for this core_methodology element is empty.
findings.proposed_fix: Restructure node features to (N, P, F_node) with one feature vector per timestamp. Run the GNN encoder P times (once per context timestamp) producing embeddings of shape (N, P, D). For the K forecast steps, either repeat the last embedding or omit GNN embeddings. This requires changes to GraphDeepAR.forward and the node feature construction in training.py.

findings.description: The Student's t-distribution NLL normalization constant uses df.mean() (line 99: `torch.tensor(math.pi * df.mean(), device=df.device)`) which averages degrees of freedom across the batch. The correct formula requires per-element df in the term -0.5*log(pi*df). This produces incorrect normalization for elements whose df differs from the batch mean, and the gradient of the loss with respect to each element's df is computed based on the batch mean rather than the element's own df. The Student-t log-likelihood formula is: log p(y) = log Gamma((df+1)/2) - log Gamma(df/2) - 0.5*log(pi*df) - log(sigma) - (df+1)/2 * log(1 + ((y-mu)/sigma)^2/df).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `torch.tensor(math.pi * df.mean(), device=df.device)` with `torch.tensor(math.pi, device=df.device) * df` to use per-element df in the normalization constant.

checks_summary.note: forecast() returns ForecastResult with distribution_params (mu, sigma, df) and Monte Carlo samples (num_samples, N, K).
Training loop iterates over time windows (t = context_length; while t+K <= train_end); all articles in each batch share the same time window t.
build_article_graph implements Eq. (1) correctly: pairwise cosine similarity via features@features.T / (norms@norms.T).
_GCNEncoder implements Eq. (2): mean-pool then W then LeakyReLU is mathematically equivalent to W then mean-pool then LeakyReLU by linearity of the linear transform W.
GNN produces single static embedding per article, not P time-varying embeddings as paper specifies (G_i in R^{D x P}).
Two-layer LSTM outputs Student-t params (mu, sigma, df). Note: df is learned as a third output; paper mentions only (mu, s^2) — reasonable extension.
Training loop uses synchronized batching; all articles in a batch share the same time window.
Graph built from pairwise cosine similarity of static features with threshold-based edge creation (0.95).
Random neighbor sampling implemented in _sample_neighbors (model.py) with max_neighbors cap.
Single Adam optimizer and Student-t NLL loss; backpropagation flows through both GNN encoder and LSTM decoder.
Node features include P demand lags + in-degree; static article features excluded from node features.
NLL normalization constant uses df.mean() instead of per-element df (training.py line 99).

caveats.text: The decoder learns degrees of freedom (df) as a third output parameter via a 3-dimensional output projection, while the paper only mentions outputting mean mu and variance s^2. The paper likely used a fixed df value (commonly df=4 for retail demand). Learning df is a reasonable extension that improves the model's flexibility and does not contradict the paper's probabilistic forecasting approach.

disclosure_request.note: Decoder outputs learned df parameter; paper likely used fixed df. Reasonable extension.

caveats.text: The GNN encoder does not include self-loops in the adjacency matrix (method.py line 72: np.fill_diagonal(adjacency, 0)). Isolated nodes (no neighbors) receive zero embeddings after the first GNN layer because the mean-pool over an empty neighbor set yields zeros. This matches the paper's Eq. (2) formula (empty sum = 0) but affects 3% of retail articles and 42% of e-commerce articles that have no neighbors.

disclosure_request.note: GNN has no self-loops; isolated nodes get zero embeddings. Matches paper's formula.

caveats.text: The optimizer substitutes Adam for the paper's Ranger optimizer (RAdam + Lookahead). This is declared as an approved approximation in the spec's blockers section and does not affect the architecture.

disclosure_request.note: Adam used instead of Ranger optimizer; approved approximation per spec.
